audit.whatIsWrong: The last three rows of the level chart disagreed between layers. Full: Skill/Skill/Skill for Level 6, First item and 2+ items. Content and packet: Anivia/Azir/Anivia.
audit.why: Glacial Storm is an instant wave-clear Azir cannot contest, so Level 6 is Anivia's. The first-item row belongs to Azir because Emperor's Divide is a 120s knockback that can shove her out of her own storm and no first item answers it. The last row returns to Anivia, whose wall cuts the line Shifting Sands has to travel.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side to Anivia, phases[5].side to Azir, phases[6].side to Anivia, with each phases[N].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] read 'Azir's shurima's legacy or first burst item', treating the passive as a poke spike, and mid called Emperor's Divide an all-in burst whose 'engage burst outclasses yours'.
audit.why: Shurima's Legacy lets him summon the Disc of the Sun from turret ruins — it is not a laning poke tool. Emperor's Divide summons a wall of soldiers that knocks back and damages; there is no burst and no stun in it. Its real threat is displacement, on a 120/105/90s cooldown at only 250 range.
audit.corrected: spikes[2], whys[5], mid and dontsFull[2] rewritten around the knockback and its cooldown.
sources: enemy kit P and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was absent: Shifting Sands dashes to ONE OF HIS OWN SAND SOLDIERS, so Crystallize — terrain that blocks dashes — can cut the line between Azir and the soldier he means to reach. The page also never mentioned that the same ability shields him, and it invented a 'soldier stun combo' and repeated 'shuriken' poke Azir does not have.
audit.why: Azir E text: 'shields himself briefly and dashes to one of his Sand Soldiers... If he hits an enemy champion, he instantly readies a new Sand Soldier and halts his dash.' Kit flags: dash and shield. Anivia W flag: 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Nothing in Azir's kit stuns, and 'shuriken' is not one of his abilities.
audit.corrected: The wall-cuts-the-dash-line interaction written into winCon, breakdown.carry, breakdown.late, dontsFull[1], spikes[3], whys[6] and late; the shield into tradeBad, phases[3].why and breakdown.feeding; every 'shuriken' and 'stun combo' removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no numbers, and whys[1] invented 'a 2-3 second Q cooldown edge'.
audit.why: Conquering Sands is 14/12/10/8/6s — 14 seconds at rank 1, the longest early cooldown in the lane and the single most punishable thing Azir does. Arise! is 1.5s, Shifting Sands 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s, Emperor's Divide 120/105/90s.
audit.corrected: The 14s window is now the organising fact of tldr, tradeGood, dosFull[1], early and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice was the generic 'threaten Q until he burns his sidestep tool' template, which does not describe how anything in this lane works.
audit.why: Azir does not sidestep — he holds range with soldiers replaced every 1.5s at 525 range, and answers a committed stun with a shielded dash. The trade window is the downtime on Conquering Sands, and the requirement is forcing the shield out first.
audit.corrected: tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.trading and report[3] rebuilt on those two facts.

edits.before: Azir's ranged soldier attacks and shuriken poke outrange your egg-punished approach, so levels 1-2 are pure farming misery — you have no way to punish his shurima's legacy on cooldown. He can shove and roam while you're stuck last-hitting under threat of a soldier stun combo. Play passive, ward for jungle pressure, and don't waste Q trying to punish a soldier since it just gets you poked more.
edits.after: Azir's soldiers out-range everything you have at level 1, so the first two levels are farming misery. But Conquering Sands is 14s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown either of you owns early — and Arise! is only 525 range, so he has to step up to place one. Play passive, ward for jungle pressure, and spend Flash Frost on that step-up rather than on a soldier you cannot punish.

edits.before: Level 6 changes everything — your Glacial Storm zones his soldier placement and threatens burst if he steps up to poke, which finally lets you contest waves. Azir still holds the edge at 3-5 with sustained ranged pressure, but by mid game you're looking for a Q that lands on a repositioning Azir near his soldiers, since Frostbite doubles into a stunned target. Watch for his all-in around 6 when he gets Emperor's Divide — his engage burst outclasses yours if he catches you out of position.
edits.after: Level 6 changes everything — Glacial Storm clears waves outright and chills the ground his soldiers have to cover, which finally lets you contest. Azir still holds 3-5 on sustained range, but from here you hunt the moment he steps up to place a soldier at 525: stun him there and Frostbite doubles off the chill. Respect his 6 as well — Emperor's Divide is a 120s knockback rather than a burst, and its real danger is shoving you out of your own storm and cutting your team off behind a wall of soldiers.

edits.before: With Rabadon's or a control mage core, your wall splits his soldier-army wombo combos from your backline, letting your Q-E-R burst him down in isolation before he can reposition his army. Late game favors you if positioning is clean — Azir needs his full soldier setup to threaten, and your wall denies that setup during teamfights.
edits.after: Crystallize is terrain and Shifting Sands is a dash to one of his own soldiers, so a wall on that line strands him away from his army — and away from the shield the dash carries. Late game favours you if your positioning is clean: Azir needs his full soldier setup to threaten anything, and one well-placed wall denies it for the whole fight.

notes: The page attributed a 'shuriken' and a 'soldier stun combo' to Azir; he has neither, and nothing in his kit stuns. Shurima's Legacy was also being used as if it were a laning poke — it is the Disc of the Sun summoned from turret ruins. The interaction the brief's own calibration note points at (Azir's soldier attacks are the thing that matters, not Azir himself) is handled here from Anivia's side: the wall cuts the dash line to the soldier. Whether Crystallize blocks the soldiers' charge from Emperor's Divide, and whether Flash Frost's stun cancels the dash mid-flight, are not answerable from the kit data and were not asserted. diff was left at TRICKY 7/10 despite a 52.89% win rate over 380 games, because unlike the akshan case the chart is genuinely mixed (three rows to Anivia, three to Azir, one skill) and the lane is execution-heavy — flagged here rather than silently changed.
